AMZN’s 2024-Q1 print shows a clear quality upgrade: revenue grew **+13% YoY ex-FX** to **$143.3B**, but the more tradeable signal is the step-change in profitability and cash generation—**operating income $15.3B (+221% YoY)** and **TTM FCF $48.8B (+$53.2B YoY)**—indicating operating leverage is now flowing through after prior cost resets. Mix is improving: **Advertising +24% YoY** (high margin) and **AWS re-accelerating to +17.2% from +13.2% in Q4** support a higher multiple narrative and reduce reliance on lower-margin retail growth.

Versus peers, the provided dataset is asymmetric, but AMZN stands out for *quantified* profit/FCF inflection while peers show mainly AI adoption metrics. On AI, AMZN’s “multibillion-dollar” gen-AI run rate plus broad Bedrock/SageMaker traction suggests AWS can sustain re-acceleration, which historically has been the key swing factor for consolidated margins.

Macro is mixed: inflation near ~3% with a **5.33%** policy rate and **4.16%** Treasury yield keeps discount rates elevated, which can cap near-term multiple expansion. However, low unemployment supports consumer demand, and AMZN’s margin/FCF momentum can offset rate pressure.

Bull case: sustained AWS re-acceleration + ads strength + durable cost discipline. Bear case: FX/geopolitics, demand sensitivity if rates stay higher for longer, and any AWS re-deceleration (the main downside catalyst). Net: constructive bias with risk tied to macro/rates and cloud growth durability.

AMZN’s 2024-Q2 print reinforces a broad-based re-acceleration with unusually strong operating leverage. Revenue of $148B (+11% YoY ex-FX) is supported by both North America (+9%) and International (+10%), suggesting demand is not narrowly concentrated; the ~100 bps leap-day benefit is a modest tailwind but doesn’t explain the full growth profile. More important for trading is the profitability/cash inflection: operating income of $14.7B (+91% YoY) and trailing-12-month adjusted FCF of $51.4B (+664% YoY) signal a step-change in efficiency and capital intensity, which typically expands valuation support during higher-rate regimes.

Relative to peers, disclosed metrics make AMZN look like a cash-generation outlier (peer data lacks comparable FCF), while Microsoft appears stronger on reported AI customer penetration. Within AMZN, AWS is the key momentum lever: growth accelerated to 18.8% from 17.2% QoQ, aligning with improving cloud demand and AI attach. Higher-margin mix is also improving via Advertising (TTM >$50B; +$2B YoY increase) and Prime Video monetization (ad-free add-on), which can further support margin durability.

Macro is mixed: inflation near ~3% and policy rates ~5.33 keep discount rates elevated (a headwind to long-duration multiples), but low unemployment supports consumer spend and ad budgets. Bull case: sustained AWS acceleration + advertising scale + structurally higher FCF. Bear case: rate sensitivity, any cloud re-deceleration, and execution risk in AI monetization versus peers.

The most actionable operating signal is AWS: +20.2% YoY growth on a $132B run-rate, paired with a very large $200B backlog, points to durable multi-quarter revenue visibility and positions AMZN well in the AI infrastructure cycle.

Margins are the key debate for trading. Reported operating income fell to $17.4B, but adjusted operating income >$21B implies underlying expansion and a return to roughly 2024-Q4 earnings power despite lower revenue—bullish if investors look through specials. Still, AMZN’s disclosed infrastructure scaling (power capacity additions and Trainium2 traction) is a relative positive for AI monetization.

Macro (policy rate ~4.3%, unemployment ~4.3%) is not restrictive enough to break demand, but higher-for-longer keeps valuation sensitivity elevated. Net: bullish on AWS-led growth and adjusted margin trajectory; cautious on event/charge risk and rate-driven multiple compression.
